DRAIN_TRANSITION_COUNT_PROXY.observed_by_blue: Yes, in the same artifact revision Blue reviewed.
DRAIN_TRANSITION_COUNT_PROXY.resolution: per-cause and per-state tallies replaced by the sorted set of causes and states observed; find_count_proxies matches drain and capture keys on the full path
DRAIN_TRANSITION_COUNT_PROXY.scenario: The first rodage artifact published transition_causes.DRAIN_COMPLETED and transition_states.DRAINING as integers. The drain path completes once per acquired filing, so both were the filing count under another name. The first count-proxy detector missed them because their key names contain no reference to filings.
DRAIN_TRANSITION_COUNT_PROXY.violates: no filing counts on a published surface

FIREWALL_TIER_CONTRACT_OVERSTATED.note: No new exposure: this is a contract-clarity defect that explains the previous two, not an additional disclosure.
FIREWALL_TIER_CONTRACT_OVERSTATED.resolution: renamed to sec_operator_internal_journals() with the guarantee stated exactly: no identifying content, volume inferable, not publishable as they stand. The no-count rule binds the published projection - status surface, Chief Brief, telemetry, observation audit and committed artifacts - which a test now holds to it.
FIREWALL_TIER_CONTRACT_OVERSTATED.scenario: paths.sec_firewall_safe_journals() was documented as "capture state a protocol-mutating surface is allowed to read", and the scheduler and attempt journals were in it. Those journals carry no filing-identifying string, but they are per-event records and some events are one per filing, so counting DRAIN_COMPLETED transitions or FILING attempts recovers the filing count. The name asserted a guarantee the contents did not provide, which is how a per-cause tally reached a published artifact without anyone noticing it was a filing count.
FIREWALL_TIER_CONTRACT_OVERSTATED.violates: the distinction between "contains no identifying content" and "publishable to a protocol-mutating actor"
